rows.existingPeriod: For a New Liberty, Murray Rothbard, 1973

recommendedAxes.reason: VIII.2 makes all land rent common while preserving titles and improvements; IX.4 adds public infrastructure. This is an economy-wide land/resource rule with mixed capital ownership, supporting moderate public orientation rather than public predominance.
IX.1 removes production/exchange taxes generally; IX.4 limits directive government while permitting cooperative provision. Moderate market coordination, not abolition of public institutions.
VIII.2 abolishes all taxes except land values and IX.1 expressly condemns customs barriers. Strong openness is a fiscal-rule prescription, not a forecast or a later-book transfer.
The private productive-property principle is general and conditioned by competition; monopoly power warrants restriction. Moderate private orientation, not unrestricted ownership.
A general price system and voluntary contracts replace productive directives; anti-monopoly, income and environmental corrections remain. This is a whole economic process rule, not an agency mandate.
The general principle expressly rejects import bans; open supply and demand support openness with narrow exceptions. Moderate, not absolute, commercial openness.

rows.existingPeriod: Escola de Freiburg, programa de Eucken/Böhm/Großmann-Doerth e princípios de Eucken (1936–1952).

recommendedAxes.reason: Equal electoral and contestatory access, independent effective popular control and protection against wealth capture are constitutive institutional requirements. Strong democratic orientation does not entail constant direct decisions.

Basic liberties require equally applied public-law protection against arbitrary private and public power. Controlled coercion remains legitimate, supporting moderate liberty rather than abolition of coercion.
